documents.title: Press Release - CPCL Financial Performance For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026
Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Press Release / Media Release

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported strong operational and financial performance for Q4 and full year FY26, delivering its highest ever annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT (112% capacity utilization). Full year Gross Refining Margin (GRM) reached $9.20/bbl, outperforming the Singapore benchmark of $5.83/bbl, while Q4 GRM stood at $13.75/bbl. Net debt stood at INR 973 crores with a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.09, and total dividends for the year hit a record INR 62 per share. Looking ahead, the company is progressing with an INR 1,600 crore Group 2/3 LOBS project and expanding its retail outlet presence. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT for FY 2024-25, representing 99.5% capacity utilization.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects to spend approximately INR 500 crores annually in normal capex.
guidance.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

guidance.claim: The company expects its INR 2,000 crore major project outlay to be executed over two to three years.
guidance.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

guidance.claim: Management expects an ongoing refinery debottlenecking study to be completed in FY27.
guidance.quote: But in the coming year, '26-'27, we hope that ongoing study will get completed.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects regular maintenance CAPEX for the next two years to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
guidance.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

guidance.claim: CPCL's refinery crude unit 1 catering to lubes is scheduled for maintenance around August or September 2025.
guidance.quote: In 2025, our refinery crude unit 1 which caters to lubes will go into maintenance around August, September.

demand_outlook.claim: CPCL strategically procures 55% to 60% of its crude requirements through long-term agreements.
demand_outlook.quote: Due to our flexible crude-sourcing mechanism, we have strategically secured 55% to 60% through long-term agreements, the remaining on short-term basis from diverse sources, allowing us to enhance flexibility and capitalize on price economies irrespective of what situation we are in.

demand_outlook.claim: Around 90% to 92% of CPCL's products are sold to Indian Oil Corporation Limited.
demand_outlook.quote: See, 90% of my product is sold to Indian Oil — around 90% to 92%.

demand_outlook.claim: The southern Indian market faces an MS product shortfall of close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: Growth in MS demand in the southern market is projected at 4%-5%, while HSD growth is forecasted at 3%.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL incurred a capex of INR 856 crores in FY26 compared to INR 673 crores in FY25.
capex_expansion.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL's retail outlet project entails a capex of INR 400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL doubled its pharma-grade Hexane capacity from 30 to 60.
capex_expansion.quote: It was 30, now the capacity is 60.

capex_expansion.claim: The new LOBS unit will add 250 KTPA of fresh Group 2 and Group 3 capacity.
capex_expansion.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL spent Rs. 673 crores on CAPEX during FY 2024-25.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the CBR project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL has full custody of 1,200 acres of land for the CBR project.
capex_expansion.quote: So, about 600 acres, which was already with CPCL and another 600 acres, which was acquired in the process, both is in our possession and the pre-project activities of boundary wall construction, and all those things are almost at a big stage.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL completed a project for 1.04 MW capacity ground-mounted and rooftop solar system on plant area buildings.
capex_expansion.quote: • 1.04 MW capacity of Ground Mounted and Roof top solar system on plant area buildings

margins_costs.claim: Q4 FY26 GRM reached $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: Core GRM for Q4 FY26 was $10.3 per barrel.
Forex losses stood at approximately INR 200 crores for Q4 FY26 and INR 350 crores for the full year.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL registered a full-year GRM of $4.22 per barrel for FY 2024-25 compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL recorded a Q4 GRM of $6.22 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $3.1 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: On Quarter 4, our GRM was $6.22 per barrel. Again, if I compare the previous year same quarter, it was $7.7 per barrel, but if I compare it to Singapore benchmark, which was only $3.1 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL recorded its best Energy Intensity Index figure of 87.4 in FY 2024-25.
margins_costs.quote: The best EII figure of 87.4 has been clocked in the current year, 2024-25.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL's core GRM stood at $3.75 per barrel for 9M 2024-25 compared to $8.21 per barrel in 2023-24.
Net operating expenditure was Rs 945 crore for 9M 2024-25 compared to Rs 1,215 crore in 2023-24.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a record annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, operating at 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: Q4 FY26 crude throughput reached 2.93 MMT, equivalent to 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL recorded a historic high distillate yield of 79.1% during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

orders_capacity.claim: Annual LPG production reached a record level of 447 TMT.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT, overcoming previous record of 404 set in 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT in FY 2024-25, representing 99.5% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year and if you take that into consideration , you will find that this performance is quite comparable to the previous year's performance where CPCL clocked 111% capacity utilization and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL's Manali Refinery has a refining capacity of 10.5 MMTPA.
CPCL reported crude throughput of 7,480 TMT for 9M 2024-25 compared to 11,642 TMT in 2023-24.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL reduced its gross debt-to-equity ratio to 0.18 from 0.39 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: Net borrowings stood at INR 973 crores with a net debt ratio of 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL announced a total dividend of INR 62 per share for FY26, comprising an interim dividend of INR 8 and a final dividend of INR 54.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's debt equity ratio stood at 0.39 with an absolute debt of Rs. 3,100 crores as of March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year. At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share for the financial year.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL held cash and bank balances of Rs 198 crore as of December 31, 2024.

risks_headwinds.claim: Logistical constraints and crude oil price volatility create operational challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Short-term disturbances affected 30% to 40% of Middle East crude supplies.
risks_headwinds.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

risks_headwinds.claim: Volatility in crude prices presents an ongoing operational challenge.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

risks_headwinds.claim: Exchange variation loss stood at Rs 122 crore for 9M 2024-25 compared to Rs 72 crore in 2023-24.
CST under recovery was Rs 246 crore for 9M 2024-25 compared to Rs 361 crore in 2023-24.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL expects to see a significant number of retail outlets commissioned in FY27.
management_commitments.quote: And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL expects its ongoing secondary debottlenecking study to be completed in FY27.
management_commitments.quote: But in the coming year, '26-'27, we hope that ongoing study will get completed.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL expects normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

management_commitments.claim: Refinery crude unit 1 will go into maintenance around August or September 2025.
management_commitments.quote: In 2025, our refinery crude unit 1 which caters to lubes will go into maintenance around August, September.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
